dedupe_keys.name: cpuc post disaster coordination and reporting rules for utilities and telecom providers california 2021

description: On 21 October 2021 the California Public Utilities Commission adopted new post-disaster community engagement and reporting requirements for investor-owned utilities and telecommunications service providers, in response to complaints from wildfire-affected communities about slow restoration of telecom services. The requirements apply after disasters declared by the Governor of California or the President, including wildfires: utilities must give the CPUC damage information within 15 days of being allowed into the disaster area, meet the impacted community in person within 30 days of being permitted back and send a summary of activities within 60 days after service is restored. Providers are also asked to consider installing fibre or fibre conduit when rebuilding community networks, electric utilities may collaborate with communities lacking high-speed Internet to build broadband, and the decision sets eligibility rules for a Digital Divide Account of USD 1 million in pilot grants. Producer: the CPUC news office, quoting Commissioners Darcie Houck and Martha Guzman Aceves. Coverage: California. Access: a public press release. Licence and cost: free to read. Caveats: this is a summary of a regulatory decision, not an outage dataset, and the page does not mention specific fires or outage counts; the full decision must be read for details. Simulation uses: the timelines and reporting duties inform recovery-time and restoration assumptions in telecom resilience models. Related record: the FCC report on the 2017 hurricane season communications (case_study-fcc-2017-hurricane-season-communications).
